NoteTexAccessor::matrix_norm¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::matrix_norm() const

Rewrite Delimited Matrix Environments To matrix¶

matrix_norm() rewrites every \begin{...}/\end{...} pair for the six bracketed amsmath matrix environments — bmatrix, pmatrix, Bmatrix, vmatrix, Vmatrix, and smallmatrix — to the plain, delimiter-free matrix environment. Use it to compare or re-render matrix source without caring which bracket style the author chose.

Only the environment markers change; the row/column content between them — including & column separators and \\ row separators — is copied unchanged. This means the rewrite discards the visual delimiters ([/] for bmatrix, (/) for pmatrix, |/| for vmatrix, and so on): matrix_norm() is for structural comparison, not for producing a bracket-equivalent rendering. Any other environment name — array, tabular, a custom matrix environment — is not recognized and passes through untouched.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Two Different Bracket Styles¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note(
    {"\\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\\0&1\\end{pmatrix} and "
     "\\begin{vmatrix}a&b\\\\c&d\\end{vmatrix}"})
    .tex().matrix_norm()
    << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{matrix}1&0\\\\0&1\\end{matrix} and \\begin{matrix}a&b\\\\c&d\\end{matrix}"]

The & column separators and \\ row separator inside each environment are untouched; only the \begin{...}/\end{...} markers change.

Example 2: An Unrecognized Environment Is Untouched¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\begin{Bmatrix}x\\end{Bmatrix}", "no matrix here"})
              .tex().matrix_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{matrix}x\\end{matrix}", "no matrix here"]

Example 3: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().matrix_norm().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().matrix_norm();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • vector_norm: the equivalent canonicalization for vector notation.

  • envs / env_names: inventory environments generically rather than rewriting a fixed set of matrix names.
